7. Mr. Chandi Charan Paul, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in view of the fact that the two sons of the admitted co-sharer Nitya Gopal Biswas have subsisting interest at least to the extent of decimal of land in the case jote but they have not being impleaded in the case, and as such the case is clearly bad for defect of parties and consequently the learned court of appeal below clearly erred in law in allowing pre-emption, in relation of the mandatory provision of section 91(1) of the Slate Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 1950 and on this ground along the impugned judgment is liable to be set in the interest of justice. Mr. Pal further submits that the learned Courts below also erred in law in not allowing improvement cost to the petition-er arbitrarily and the same has accessioned failure of justice. 

 14. Mr. Pal has referred to me the case of Abdus Saker and others vs. Md. Sohrab All and others reported in 33 DLR (AD) 1130 in support of his submission. Mr. Pal has also referred to the case of Harun Miah Vs. Mvi. Majid Uddin Ahmed Chowdhury and others reported in 4 DLR, 114, the case of Sonaulla Howlader Vs. 4fser Uddin Bali and others reported in 7 DLR, 514, the case of Mahaprabhu Ram Vs. Copal Ram and others reported in 42 DLR (AD) 154, the case of Syed Abdul Karim and another Vs. Harendra Chandra Dhupi and others reported in 14 DLR, 847 and the case of Feroza Majid and another Vs. Jiban Bima Corporation reported in 39 DLR (AD) 78 in support of his contention. In these cited cases the importance of impleading necessary parties in a pre-emption application has been highlighted. There is no dispute to the proposition of law laid down in these decisions, which is clearly envisaged in section 96(1) of the S.A.T. Act, 1950. There is thus no dispute to the proposition that a co-sharer tenant or the holder of a land contiguous to the case land is a necessary party in a pre-emption case filed by a co-sharer tanent or by a contiguous land-holder, as the case many be and his presence is essential for complete and effectu-al adjudication of the case. But in our case under review the pre-emptors definite case is that after his sales as evidenced by Ext. 3 and 3 (ka) in 1974 Nitya Gopal Biswas was left with no subsisting interest in the case jote and the pre-emptee led evidence to substantiate the said fact. The learned courts below on considered of the evidence on record concurrently found that Nitya Copal Biswas had no subsisting interest in the case jote after his sales vide Ext. 3 and 3 (ka).
